Effects of estrogen: Estradiol (E2) is a sex-hormone and a type of estrogen involved in the menstrual cycle. It is mainly produced by the ovarian follicles and by the corpus luteum. Its major role in the menstrual cycle is to act as a growth hormone for reproducitve organs, supports the lining of the endometrium. During the menstruation, the level of estrogen is too low to maintain the endometrium, causing its functional layer to shed.
Effects of progesterone:
The main role of progesterone is to prepare the uterus for fertilization and make it receptive for implantation. It is mainly produced by the corpus luteum, in the luteal phase.
The level of progesterone is too low to maintain the endometrium stable, causing it to shed.
Effects of FSH:
The main role of the follicle-stimulating hormone, or FSH, is to support ovarian follicles growth. It is produced by the anterior pituitary as a reponse to GnRH (gonadotropin-releasing hormone).
GnRH is released by the hypothalamus, triggering the production of FSH by the anterior pituitary. This stimulates the development of several ovarian follicles.
Effects of LH: Luteinizing hormone, or LH, mainly acts on ovarian tissue, it contributes to the development of ovarian follicle and is the key trigger for ovulation. It is produced by the anterior pituitary as a reponse to GnRH (gonadotropin-releasing hormone). The level of LH is low during menstruation but increases gradually as hypothalamus releases GnRH which triggers the anterior pituitary to release LH.
Energy Levels Type: You might be experiencing low energy and tiredness. This time calls for rest and recovery and gentle exercises.
Type of food: During the menstrual phase it is best to eat foods with high iron and high vitamin B. Some examples include red mean, poultry, fish, leafy greens and nuts and seeds.
Example of Food: For further information on the types of food and recipes you can make dependent on the phase you are in,you can find it here. https://femia.health/health-library/your-cycle/health/cycle-syncing-diet/#elementor-toc__heading-anchor-3
Concentration Levels: You might find it harder to concentrate and harder time processing information.
Health aspect: This can vary depending on the person. The average is 5 days. This can vary, and the duration of your cycle might change from the average 28 day cycle. The average blood loss is 30mL, if you see that you lose more than 80mL contact doctor
Mood: During this time you might feel low and easily irritable. As well as feeling the need for more comfort than usual.
Types of Vitamins: Recommended to take some iron, vitamin C and magnesium. Please check with your doctors beforehand.
What is happening in the Brain: Hypothalamus releases GnRH (gonadotropin-releasing hormone) which stimulates the anterior pituitary to produce FSH and LH.
What's happening in the Ovaries: Rising level of FSH stimulates the development of several ovarian follicles. No dominant follicle is yet observable, they are all competing.
What is happening in the Uterus: The low amount of estrogens and progesterones cannot maintain the stability of the endometrium anymore, causing the uterine lining to shed blood and tissues : this is the menstrual flow.
What is happening in each phase: It is the start of a new menstrual cycle. The body re-prepares itself for a future possible fertilization : the lining of the uterus is shed through the vagina and ovarian follicles start their development.

Effects of estrogen: Estradiol (E2) is a sex hormone and a type of estrogen involved in the menstrual cycle. It is mainly produced by the ovarian follicles and by the corpus luteum. Its major role in the menstrual cycle is to act as a growth hormone for reproducitve organs, supports the lining of the endometrium. The development of the ovarian follicles increases the level of estrogen. It rebuilts the endometrium, preparing the uterus for fertilization.  The increasing level of estrogen also produces a negative feedback on the brain, causing it to produce less FSH and LH, ovarian follicles stop their development, and one becomes dominant. Later in this phase, the high level of estrogen switches the feedback from negative to positive, causing a surge of LH necessary for the ovulation.
Effects of progesterone:
The main role of progesterone is to prepare the uterus for fertilization and make it receptive for implantation. It is mainly produced by the corpus luteum, in the luteal phase.
The level of progesterone stays low.
Effects of FSH: The main role of the follicle-stimulating hormone, or FSH, is to support ovarian follicles growth. It is produced by the anterior pituitary as a reponse to GnRH (gonadotropin-releasing hormone). The level of FSH decreases because of the negative feedback from estrogen. The development of follicles slows down and one follicle becomes dominant.
Effects of LH: Luteinizing hormone, or LH, mainly acts on ovarian tissue, it contributes to the development of ovarian follicle and is the key trigger for ovulation. It is produced by the anterior pituitary as a reponse to GnRH (gonadotropin-releasing hormone). The level of LH is rising, it supports the development of growing ovarian follicles.
Energy Levels Type: You might feel more refreshed and physically stronger. Now is the perfect time for high intensity workouts.
Type of food: Throughout the follicular phase it is recommended that you eat a balanced diet to support hormonal balance and to boost your energy levels. Examples include fresh fruits, vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins and healthy fats.
Example of Food: For further information on the types of food and recipes you can make dependent on the phase you are in,you can find it here. https://femia.health/health-library/your-cycle/health/cycle-syncing-diet/#elementor-toc__heading-anchor-3
Concentration Levels: In early follicular phase you will be feeling foggier and might feel slower. Right before ovulation you will feel the sharpest and be at peak performance.
Health aspect: The follicular phase can vary depending on the person, if your full cycle is longer than 35 days or below 21, contact your doctor.
Mood: Throughout the follicular phase your mood levels will increase due to the increase in seratonin. You might feel more optimistic, social and have a positive outlook.
Types of Vitamins: Recommended to take Vitamin B, Omega 3 and zinc. Please check with your doctors beforehand.
What is happening in the Brain: The rising level of estrogen produces a negative feedback on the hypothalamus / anterior pituitary system that decreases the production of FSH and LH. Later in the follicular phase, when the level of estrogen is sufficiently high, it switches the feedback from a negative to a positive one, producing a LH surge triggering ovulation.
What's happening in the Ovaries: Multiple follicles develop, then one becomes dominant and the others regress. This dominant follicle produces high amount of estrogens.
What is happening in the Uterus: The uterus is in proliferative state: the increasing level of estrogen thickens the endometrium, the functional layer is regenerated and cervical mucus becomes thinner and more elastic. It prepares the uterus for a possible implantation.
What is happening in each phase: One of the multiple ovarian follicles becomes dominant. The uterus prepares for a possible implantation.

Effects of estrogen: Estradiol (E2) is a sex-hormone and a type of estrogen involved in the menstrual cycle. It is mainly produced by the ovarian follicles and by the corpus luteum. Its major role in the menstrual cycle is to act as a growth hormone for reproductive organs, supports the lining of the endometrium.The high level of estrogen at the end of the follicular phase produces a positive feedback on the brain that produces a surge of LH and a smaller amount of FSH, which allows for the release of the rupture of the dominant follicle.
Effects of progesterone:
The main role of progesterone is to prepare the uterus for fertilization and make it receptive for implantation. It is mainly produced by the corpus luteum in the luteal phase.
The levels of progesterone is low.
Effects of FSH:
The main role of the follicle-stimulating hormone, or FSH, is to support ovarian follicles growth. It is produced by the anterior pituitary as a response to GnRH (gonadotropin-releasing hormone).
There is a surge of FSH caused by a high amount of estrogen. This surge is minor compared to the surge in LH, which is the main trigger for ovulation.
Effects of LH: Luteinizing hormone, or LH, mainly acts on ovarian tissue; it contributes to the development of ovarian follicles and is the key trigger for ovulation. It is produced by the anterior pituitary as a reponse to GnRH (gonadotropin-releasing hormone). The high amount of estrogen produces a positive feedback that triggers a sharp peak in the amount of LH. It triggers ovulation : the dominant follicle, the oocyte is released from the ovary into the fallopian tube.
Energy Levels Type: At ovulation you will feel at the peak of your energy levels. This is the perfect time for endurance based exercises and participating in competitive sports.
Type of food: Eat foods with high fiber and antioxidants to support ovulation and reproductive health. Some key foods to eat during the ovulation phase include lean meats, eggs, avocados, vegetables and nuts and berries.
Example of Food: For further information on the types of food and recipes you can make dependent on the phase you are in,you can find it here. https://femia.health/health-library/your-cycle/health/cycle-syncing-diet/#elementor-toc__heading-anchor-3
Concentration Levels: Highest memory and attention span right before ovulation. You will be at your peak.
Mood: You will feel at your best, you will be the most outgoing and social and emotionally resilient. However depending per individual the change in hormones might result in sensitivity or moodswings, or anxiety.
Types of Vitamins: Recommended to take Vitamin B, Omega 3 and zinc. Please check with your doctors beforehand.
What is happening in the Brain: The high amount of estrogen creates a positive feedback that stimulates the anterior pituitary to produce a LH surge and a smaller FSH surge.
What's happening in the Ovaries: There is a rupture of the dominant follicle, the oocyte is released into the Fallopian tube, and the ruptured follicle transforms into the corpus luteum.
What is happening in the Uterus: The uterus is prepared for a possible implantation.
What is happening in each phase: A LH surge triggers ovulation: the oocyte is released into the Fallopian tube and transitions into the corpus luteum.

Effects of estrogen: Estradiol (E2) is a sex hormone and a type of estrogen involved in the menstrual cycle. It is mainly produced by the ovarian follicles and by the corpus luteum. Its major role in the menstrual cycle is to act as a growth hormone for reproductive organs, supporting the lining of the endometrium. The corpus luteum produces a moderate amount of estrogen.
Effects of progesterone:
The main role of progesterone is to prepare the uterus for fertilization and make it receptive for implantation. It is mainly produced by the corpus luteum, in the luteal phase.
The corpus luteum produces progesterone, which becomes the dominant hormone. Progesterone helps the endometrium to become receptive to implantation. It also produces a negative feedback on the brain, decreasing the production of LH and FSH.
Effects of FSH:
The main role of the follicle-stimulating hormone, or FSH, is to support ovarian follicles growth. It is produced by the anterior pituitary as a reponse to GnRH (gonadotropin-releasing hormone).
The level of FSH decreases because of the negative feedback caused by progesterone. This prevents furter development of ovarian follicles.
Effects of LH: Luteinizing hormone, or LH, mainly acts on ovarian tissue, it contributes to the development of ovarian follicle and is the key trigger for ovulation. It is produced by the anterior pituitary as a reponse to GnRH (gonadotropin-releasing hormone). As progesterone becomes the dominant hormone, it triggers a negative feedback that reduces the production of LH.
Energy Levels Type: You may still experience high energy from ovulation, still making it easier for high intensity activities.
Type of food: In the luteal phase it is best to eat foods rich with healthy proteins, magnesium, zinc and vitamin B. Some examples of these foods are dark chocolate, healthy proteins such as chicken and fish, vegetables, leafy greens and legumes.
Example of Food: For further information on the types of food and recipes you can make dependent on the phase you are in,you can find it here. https://femia.health/health-library/your-cycle/health/cycle-syncing-diet/#elementor-toc__heading-anchor-3
Concentration Levels: You will find it easiest for deep thinking, emotional reflection and social sensitivity.
Health aspect: This will always be 14 days. However if you notice a great difference of the length, for example a length of 10 days for the phase, then please contact your doctor as it may be a symptom to other health diseases.
Mood: The change in the hormones will result in mood swings, irritation and symptoms of PMS. During this time you might feel sad, angry and easily irrited. You might also feel more overwhelmed and less sociable.
Types of Vitamins: Recommended to take magnesium, vitamin B6 and zinc. Please check with your doctors beforehand.
What is happening in the Brain: Progesterone becomes the dominant hormone, it produces a negative feedback on brain, decreasing the production of LH and FSH.
What's happening in the Ovaries: The ruptured follicles transition into the corpus luteum which produces a high amount of progesterone.
What is happening in the Uterus: The uterus is prepared for a possible implantation.
What is happening in each phase: The corpus luteum produces progesterones, it decreases the production of LH and FSH and prepares the uterus to welcome the implantation.
